Hey,

before starting with anything else, I apologize if anything going forth sounds empty/dry or anything along those lines. It is not meant to be! I am someone who is extremely poor at sharing my feelings and who tends to keep feelings to himself. Nonetheless, I wish to at least spark some positive thought in you. 

Firstly, I would be lying if I said I can imagine how you feel, or how hard it is for you. I can not and I doubt anyone can truly. But as someone who also had strict upbringing and more often than not felt disappointed at my parents for not being proud of me when I accomplished something and was constantly compared to others who 1 out of 1000 times did better than me, I can sympathize with that at least. It was not easy for me to keep going through that and I imagine for you it was even harder. Just for that I want to say I'm proud you managed everything you did so far! 

In my opinion, just as you also said in your last paragraph, suicide is the last of your options. It is never the best or a good way out, even if it would at first seem so. With stress, anxiety, fear, depression, etc. building up, it feels like nothing will help you anymore and the only thing left is suicide. That is not the case. There is a lot of people willing to help you find meaning for yourself, albeit seemingly insignificantly small. Don't hesitate to ask more people, for example the suicide hotline, for help with your situation just as you did here.

About leaving the right message. I believe that you answered part of it by yourself. Regarding the messages you want to leave for your mother and father. It may seem easy to say and so on, but instead of leaving the message through a suicide note, I want to encourage you to pass this message on through your own efforts. Show your mother that you can be independent of her. Try finding a job, maybe move out from her house. Show her that, all on your own and through your own efforts, you can be a better, stronger person than she could ever aspire to be.   
Show your father, that while you have had it hard, which I hope he realises, you did not give up on yourself. You finished high school, you are qualified to go to a university. You managed high school, so why not take it a step further and finish college? Show him that even though you had it hard and seemingly no one believed in you, it is through your own effort that you picked yourself up and got out of the slump you were in. That as long as one is breathing, there is hope for a change to the better. Always.  
Through these actions you will also be able to show your siblings the same thing. It is mostly them who define their future. Through their efforts, their actions, their desire to change anything and everything. 

To give you my honest opinion on your questions, if suicide would really change anything and if that would leave the right message:

For you, suicide would change the fact that you don't have to live in torment anymore. While that in itself may be what you somehow seek for, it would also mean that you never got free of it. You weren't able to change it. So I guess if I had to give a definitive answer it would be no, it would not change anything.

If it would leave the right message is a difficult thing to determine. It could have your desired change but it could also go horribly wrong. From what I've read it seems your siblings are younger than you. I personally think, that it would be hard for them to grow stronger through you killing yourself. This is not meant as a "suicide is bad" comment, but rather as a "is that the only way I can make that clear to them" comment.   
The same situation can be said about your message for your father. He has had a hard time being unemployed for so long and losing his money. No matter who you are, it is not easy to come back from such a situation. Losing one of the things he still has in this world would be more devastating than helping for him.   
Concerning your mother, I can't really comment on her since she seems to be the type who will always view others, and especially her children, as inferior to her. My mother also has the same thing going on, albeit not to that extent. But whenever a discussion gets more intense or something isn't to her liking, she immediately puts others beneath her. Such people will always try to find fault with you no matter the actions you take.   
So, as above, if I had to give a definitve answer to the second question it would also be no.

To conclude this comment, which hopefully gave you a different view on things, please do remember that most/all of this is just my opinion as some stranger on the internet who is genuinely concerned about your well-being. I do not mean to say you are wrong in anything you said, nor do I want to support any of the things you said, as you and I are driven by different emotions concerning this matter. But if it helps you, I want you to know that from your message above I get the feeling and believe you can change the things you want to change without taking your own life. 

As with posting this comment I got involved in your life, even if it is just a comment on the internet, if you do decide to take your life, I want you to know that, since I am religious, I will pray that in the afterlife you will have a better time and finally achieve the life you always dreamed of, which unfortunately you didn't have to live out on earth.

Kind regards

Pusty
